title: Cause & Effect
description: Use cause and effect chains to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to cause & effect with appropriate B2 complexity.
objectives: Use cause and effect chains to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to cause & effect with appropriate B2 complexity.

stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to use cause and effect chains to structure, justify, and negotiate ideas related to cause & effect with appropriate B2 complexity. The central language focus is cause and effect chains. In the context of academic & structured communication, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At B2, organize the message so the listener can follow the claim, support, qualification, and practical consequence. Choose collocations and discourse markers that sound natural in professional and social contexts.

blocks.explanation: This model establishes the main communicative move.

blocks.english: A clear explanation addresses lead to directly.
blocks.explanation: This model develops or qualifies the message.

blocks.text: Start with the model “The discussion highlighted logical sequence.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “A clear explanation addresses lead to directly.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: cause and effect chains. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by cause and effect chains; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For cause & effect, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.
